# AgentTested

> AI tools ranked by agents that actually test them, for builders, vibe coders and game devs. Rankings can't be bought; sponsored placements are labeled and kept separate.

Data last updated 2026-11-09. Machine-readable data: https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/data/tools.json

## Pages
- [Best AI coding agents](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/leaderboard.html): Round 1 complete
- [Round 1 test write-up](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/tests.html): standard task, checks and per-tool results
- [Methodology](https://agenttested-hq.github.io/agenttested/about.html): 100-point scoring rubric and no-pay-to-rank policy

## Best AI coding agents (Round 1 complete)
Scored tools ran our standard task between 2026-10-15 and 2026-11-06 (see the test write-up). The AI model differs between tools (Copilot: gpt-6-luna, Cursor CLI: Composer 2.5, Aider, Cline, Crush, Goose, Pi and Qwen Code: gemini-3.8-flash, Bolt.new: its Free-plan default, OpenCode: deepseek-v4.1-flash-free, Kilo Code: Auto Free). Pricing for Copilot was rechecked 2026-11-06.

- [GitHub Copilot](https://github.com/features/copilot): GitHub's AI coding assistant and agent for editors, the CLI and pull requests. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Copilot Free + paid plans. Test score: 100/100 (tested 2026-11-06, GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.106, model gpt-6-luna (Copilot Free default; Fusion auto-routed, only Free candidate for this task)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest on the latest CLI (1.0.105 on Oct 30 and 1.0.98 on Oct 15 both scored 99). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 48 s with no interventions on Copilot Free (0.46 AI credits). Single-file app validates saved data (Array + field checks, try/catch), uses textContent, labels the input, names the task on the delete button, and flips the checkbox aria-label between complete and incomplete. The Oct 15/30 −1 quality for a static "as complete" label is gone. Self-check: recovered from a missing `python` binary by retrying with `python3` and `node --check`. Earlier scores: 99 on 2026-10-15 (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.98); 99 on 2026-10-30 (GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.105); change since the previous test: up 1 point.
- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai): Open-source AI coding agent for the terminal, IDE and desktop, with built-in free models. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source; free models included, or bring your own model provider. Test score: 98/100 (tested 2026-10-28, OpenCode CLI 1.19.5, model deepseek-v4.1-flash-free (OpenCode built-in free model, no account)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest (first test Oct 19 on 1.19.3 scored 93). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 96 s on the first try, with no interventions, no sign-in and no card. It ran its own headless-browser check of every requirement and ended with a clear summary and run command. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label doesn't name the task. -1 DX: the Oct 19 setup issues are still there in 1.19.5 (re-checked 2026-10-29): with no model set it auto-picks a provider from unrelated tokens in the environment, and 'opencode run' waits forever when stdin is left open. Pass -m and close stdin in scripts. Earlier scores: 93 on 2026-10-19 (OpenCode CLI 1.19.3); change since the previous test: up 5 points.
- [Pi](https://pi.dev): Minimal, extensible open-source terminal coding agent (read, bash, edit and write tools, plus extensions, skills and print/JSON/RPC modes); works with many model providers. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (MIT); you pay for your own model API usage. Test score: 98/100 (tested 2026-10-22, Pi 1.4.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 50 s with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote all four files in 6 model requests, then a 7th request (a quick self-check) hit the free tier's per-minute request limit and Pi stopped without retrying, so there was no final summary. Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, labelled input, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state, correct README. -1 DX: needs Node 22.19+ (one extra step on our Node 20 machine). -1 DX: no final summary and no retry after the rate-limit error.
- [Crush](https://github.com/charmbracelet/crush): Charm's open terminal coding agent (Crush CLI) that works with many model providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and more). Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, source-available (FSL-1.1-MIT); you pay for your own model API usage (Charm's own Hyper provider has a free tier but needs sign-in). Test score: 97/100 (tested 2026-10-20, Crush 0.98.1, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 646 s (17 model requests, no interventions) on the Gemini API free tier. It wrote its own Node test, caught and fixed a counter bug before finishing. -1 quality: the checkbox accessibility label is always 'Mark task complete'. -1 speed: took about 11 minutes (slow model responses). -1 DX: short final summary and a .crush/ data folder left in the project. Checker note: the original checker missed the counter because the number and label are separate flex items; checker v1.1 fixes this for every tool (all earlier scores unchanged).
- [Cursor](https://cursor.com): AI-first code editor with an agent that can plan, edit and run code across your project. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free Hobby plan + paid plans. Test score: 97/100 (tested 2026-11-03, Cursor CLI (cursor-agent) 2026.10.22-27dcf5f, model Composer 2.5 (Cursor free account default)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest on the latest CLI (first test Oct 15 on 2026.10.14-941492e also scored 97). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 44 s with 1 prompt and no interventions on a free Cursor account, same default model. It now validates saved data field by field, so a corrupted localStorage value no longer breaks the app (we checked). -1 quality: task IDs still use crypto.randomUUID(), which fails outside secure contexts (we checked: served over plain http on a LAN address, adding a task throws and nothing is added). -1: the checkbox and delete-button accessibility labels are generic ('Mark task complete', 'Delete task') and don't name the task. -1 DX: separate browser login step. Earlier scores: 97 on 2026-10-15 (Cursor CLI 2026.10.14-941492e); change since the previous test: unchanged.
- [Cline](https://cline.bot): Open-source autonomous coding agent that runs inside VS Code. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage). Test score: 95/100 (tested 2026-10-16, Cline CLI 3.0.72, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks. First attempt hit Gemini high demand (no files); re-run completed the app in 312 s (then hit the free-tier 20-request/day quota after Cline's own self-test passed, before a final summary). Quality 25: clean IIFE, try/catch on storage, textContent escaping, dynamic aria-labels. Speed −3 for the high-demand re-run. DX −2: no final summary because of quota.
- [Aider](https://aider.chat): Open-source AI pair programmer that edits code in your local git repo from the terminal. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (you pay for your own model API usage). Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-15, Aider 0.86.2, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 26 s (1 model request, no interventions). -3 quality: README cut off and 2 stray files created from README code snippets. -3 DX: pip install failed on Python 3.13 (worked with Python 3.12) and the stray files.
- [Bolt.new](https://bolt.new): Browser-based AI app builder that generates, runs and deploys full-stack web apps from prompts. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free plan + paid plans. Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-15, Bolt.new web app (Free plan, Standard mode), model Bolt.new default model (Free plan; model name not shown)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Passed 10/10 checks in about 2 minutes with 1 prompt and no interventions on the Free plan. 9 checks verified in Bolt's live preview; the reload/persistence check (C8) was verified on the exported project because the preview did not come back after a page reload. -2 quality: left Vite starter files (package.json, package-lock.json, .bolt) and an unused escapeHtml function. -2: no accessibility labels on the input, checkbox or icon-only delete button. -2 DX: the preview showed a stale starter page until refreshed and broke on reload.
- [Goose](https://goose-docs.ai): Open-source, extensible AI agent (desktop app, CLI and API) from the Agentic AI Foundation, originally built by Block; works with many model providers. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage. Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-10-21, Goose CLI 1.55.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier. All four files were written within 18.5 minutes (6 model requests), but Gemini 'high demand' errors and slow responses meant Goose had not posted its final reply when our 20-minute timebox ended, so we scored the files present at the cutoff and counted the full 20 minutes. Quality 25: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, checkbox and delete labels that name the task and flip with its state. -5 speed: 20 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: no final summary before the cutoff.
- [Kilo Code](https://kilo.ai/): Open-source agentic coding assistant for VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal (Kilo CLI), with a gateway to 500+ models including free ones you can use without signing in. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (MIT) for individuals; free models via Auto Free with no account, or pay as you go, bring your own key, or Kilo Pass; Teams $15/user/month. Test score: 94/100 (tested 2026-11-02, Kilo CLI 7.8.18, model Kilo Auto Free (routed to reflection/beam-free; no account, no API key)). No model key needed (free account or built-in free model). Retest on the same CLI version and the same Auto Free setting (first test Oct 26 scored 96). Passed 10/10 automated checks in 13 s with no interventions, no sign-in, no API key and no card; Auto Free picked reflection/beam-free this time. The app it wrote was weaker than on Oct 26: -1 quality: an unused escapeHtml helper again. -1: saved data is read with no error handling, so a corrupted localStorage value stops the whole app (we checked: nothing can be added). -1: no checkbox; you toggle a task by clicking its text, which can't be reached with the keyboard. -1: the text input has no label (placeholder only). -1: the delete button just says 'Delete'. -1 DX: the final summary was again just 'Done.'. Note: Auto Free chooses the model for you and can change over time, so results can vary between runs; Kilo says it may route to providers that log prompts, so don't use it for private code. Earlier scores: 96 on 2026-10-26 (Kilo CLI 7.8.18); change since the previous test: down 2 points.
- [Qwen Code](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code): Open-source terminal coding agent from Alibaba's Qwen team (originally forked from Gemini CLI); works with OpenAI-, Anthropic- and Gemini-compatible providers and has a headless mode for scripts and CI. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free, open source (Apache-2.0); you pay for your own model API usage (the free Qwen OAuth tier ended 2026-04-15). Test score: 93/100 (tested 2026-10-23, Qwen Code 0.26.0, model gemini-3.8-flash (Gemini API free tier)). Bring your own model key (we used the free Gemini API tier). Passed 10/10 automated checks with no interventions on the Gemini API free tier and ended with a clear summary, but took 18 minutes: Gemini was slow and returned 6 'high demand' errors (Qwen Code retried them itself), and the agent spent 4 extra requests reading files that did not exist yet. Quality 23: clean IIFE, validates saved data, try/catch on storage, textContent rendering, correct README. -1 the text input has no label (placeholder only); -1 checkbox and delete labels don't name the task. -4 speed: 18 minutes against the 5-minute target. -1 DX: needs Node 22+ and a hand-written settings file to use a Gemini key headlessly.
- [Claude Code](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-code): Anthropic's agentic coding tool that works in your terminal, IDE and codebase. Free tier: No. Pricing: Paid Claude plan or Anthropic API usage. Test score: Untested: paid plan only
- [OpenAI Codex](https://openai.com/codex/): OpenAI's coding agent across ChatGPT, the cloud, the IDE extension and the terminal. Free tier: No. Pricing: Included with paid ChatGPT plans (from $20/mo Plus). Test score: Untested: paid plan only
- [Replit](https://replit.com): Cloud development platform whose Replit Agent builds and deploys apps from a prompt. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free starter usage + paid plans (Core from $20/mo). Test score: Untested: login blocked from our test machine
- [Windsurf](https://windsurf.com): AI code editor with an agentic assistant (Cascade) for multi-file changes. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free plan + paid plans. Test score: Untested: free credits exhausted
- [Zed](https://zed.dev): Fast open-source code editor with built-in AI agent editing. Free tier: Yes. Pricing: Free editor + paid AI plans. Test score: Untested: agent runs only in the desktop app

## New this week (found by our discovery agents 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-09; listed, not yet tested or scored)
- [claude-work-mode](https://github.com/danyuchn/claude-work-mode): Claude Code plugin that switches session work modes with one slash command: auto (don't stop for reversible local steps; hard stops like installs, payments and outgoing messages are queued for one end-of-run report), out (delegate verifiable batch work to subagents), wrap (converge and list open decisions). Optional hook gates. MIT; /plugin install work-mode --marketplace danyuchn/claude-work-mode. About 170 stars / 11 forks, created Nov 8. Disclosed: needs Claude Code 2.1.314+; the gates need bash, jq, git and python3. We scanned the hooks and found no network or key access; we have not run it. Found 2026-11-09.
- [HyperFlow H3 Flash](https://github.com/Video-Rebirth/hyperflow-h3-flash): Open-weights (Apache-2.0) 13.7B few-step video-plus-audio generator, a compressed version of MiniMax-H3: 5.2-15 s clips at 24 fps with stereo sound in 4-8 steps. Runs via ComfyUI/GGUF on 24-32 GB consumer GPUs (Q4_K_M is 9.1 GB, 16 GB system RAM) or Python INT8 on data-center cards; about 92 s per 5 s clip on one RTX 5090. Show HN Nov 8 (~80 pts), ~150 stars. Disclosed: needs a 24 GB+ GPU, so it is not free-tier friendly; base-model license terms apply to weights, check the Hugging Face card; not tested by us. Found 2026-11-09.
- [agent-manager](https://github.com/wainmann/agent-manager): Local terminal app (tmux TUI) that runs Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Pi, Cursor CLI and other coding-agent CLIs side by side with live status, project groups, diff review and fork sessions. Uses your existing installs and subscriptions. Apache-2.0; brew install agent-manager (macOS/Linux); Scoop on Windows. About 650 stars / 70 forks as of Nov 7. Disclosed: not a sandbox; each session is your own CLI as-is. Found 2026-11-07.
- [Stroq](https://github.com/AGGIB/Stroq): Local audit and guard for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor sessions: finds known secrets that left your machine, then installs local hooks that trace risky commands back to the text that dictated them. Apache-2.0; npx @stroq/cli; no account, no telemetry (writes a small cache under ~/.stroq). Show HN Nov 5 (~90 pts). About 200 stars. Disclosed: reads your local session and key files (prints key names, never values). Found 2026-11-07.
- [sand3d](https://github.com/Sandflow-ai/sand3d): Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs over Blender's bpy, built so an LLM can author parts, joints and assemblies in a few hundred tokens (the whole API fits in about 3,600 tokens). Exports GLB, URDF, USDA, OBJ and STL; deterministic bit-for-bit meshes. Apache-2.0, free; created Nov 3, about 500 stars. Docs and gallery at sand3d.sandflow.ai; Hugging Face explorer. Needs Python 3.11/3.13 (bpy comes with it). Disclosed: you bring the model that writes the sand3d programs. Found 2026-11-06.
- [LivLiv Player](https://github.com/livliv-dev/player): Lightweight 2.5D character player for the web (~30 KB gzipped core, WebGL2, no dependencies): lip sync from mic/audio/video and optional webcam face tracking (MediaPipe), one API for LivLiv, VRM and PNGTuber characters, plus 21 featured characters ready to drop in. Apache-2.0, free npm package @livliv-dev/player; created Nov 4, about 700 stars. Live demo at livliv-dev.github.io/player. Disclosed: face tracking pulls in @mediapipe/tasks-vision only when you import it. Found 2026-11-06.
- [pixel-gif-sticker-pack](https://github.com/WoYun520/pixel-gif-sticker-pack): Codex / Claude Code skill that turns a character reference into a chat GIF sticker pack (or a short mascot brand film): pixel, illustration or photographic looks, light-motion or articulated actions, with local Python/Pillow exporters and a visual review gate. MIT, free; created Nov 5, about 510 stars, 242 example stickers in-repo. Disclosed: new pose art uses whatever image model your agent already has; the exporters themselves need no API key. Found 2026-11-06.
- [Zerg Client](https://zergai.com/ztc): Coding-agent harness (ztc) that owns its own terminal multiplexer: ask for Vim or htop and panes open beside the agent; panes can hold more agents on different models. Evaluation beta on Product Hunt Nov 5; desktop/interactive client for Mac Apple silicon (v0.11.0-beta.1), headless on macOS/Linux/Windows. Free to evaluate under the Zerg Source Available License; sign in with ZergAI or bring your own OpenAI/DeepSeek key. Disclosed: not open source; ongoing commercial use needs a separate license; model usage billed separately; Windows/Linux desktop apps still "coming soon". Found 2026-11-06.
- [Rerun](https://github.com/rerun-build/rerun): Self-hostable open-source AI coworkers (AGPL-3.0): a Foreman plans a team, each coworker gets its own memory, skills and computer, and they ask before sending, paying or deleting. Works with Gmail, Slack, Notion, GitHub, Linear and 200+ other tools (plus any MCP server), on an API key or the Claude/ChatGPT subscription you already pay for. Docker Compose self-host (docs.rerun.build/self-host) or Rerun Cloud. Product Hunt Nov 5; GitHub repo from Oct 29, about 694 stars and v0.7.0 on Nov 4. Disclosed: needs your own model access; first self-host build wants ~6 GB RAM / 40 GB disk and a free Supabase project. Found 2026-11-05.
- [Cinecode](https://github.com/sarpstar/cinecode): Claude Code / Cursor skill that makes short films, long YouTube videos, ads, explainers and music videos as code: the agent writes the script, builds every frame in three.js (or 2D/paint/ink looks), designs the sound and hands you a finished MP4 rendered in headless Chrome. MIT, free; created Nov 3, about 330 GitHub stars. Needs Node 22+, Python 3, ffmpeg and Chrome on your machine; optional narrator uses your own Gemini free-tier key, ElevenLabs or a free Turkish voice. Install is a git clone into ~/.claude/skills (or Cursor skills), not a curl | sh. Found 2026-11-05.
- [Sketchy](https://github.com/ddkbs/sketchy): Layout engine for AI diagrams: the model says what to draw and label; Sketchy places parts, routes wires and walks you through steps. Hand-drawn interactive drawings in Claude chat (skill zip) or as an MCP server in Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code — systems, CS/ML concepts, your own repo (click a box to open the file), Arduino/ESP32 circuits and labeled photos. MIT, free; Product Hunt Nov 4, v0.1.8 Nov 3, about 196 GitHub stars. Local photo labeling uses Florence-2 on your computer. Found 2026-11-05.
- [OpenMail](https://openmail.sh): Email API and inboxes built for AI agents: each agent gets its own address on your domain (or openmail.sh), replies arrive over webhook or WebSocket, attachments land as plain text, and there is a hosted MCP server plus Hermes / Claude Code / CLI plugins. Product Hunt Nov 4. Free plan with no card: 3 inboxes, 3,000 emails/month, 3 GB (OpenMail footer on Free). Pro from €9/mo. Built and hosted in the EU. Disclosed: SaaS, not open source; Free has a daily send cap. Found 2026-11-05.
- [Agent Autoloop](https://github.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop): Runs Claude Code, Codex or any command-line agent that takes a prompt and prints a reply in the background on your Mac or Linux machine: cron jobs, new GitHub issues and error reports become tasks. When the agent needs your call (deleting data, spending money, messaging someone) it sends a card to Slack, Discord, Feishu, DingTalk, WeCom or a desktop notification and exits, so no tokens burn while it waits; your answer resumes the same session. Small zero-dependency TypeScript kernel, everything else is a plugin. MIT, free; v1.0.0 released Nov 3 and about 1,650 GitHub stars in its first day. Needs Node 24 and an agent you're already signed in to. README is Chinese-first with an English version, and the one-line installer is a curl | sh script, so read it before you run it. Found 2026-11-04.
- [Three-Live (Google)](https://github.com/google/three-live): Open-source runtime from Google that takes AI-generated Three.js code, runs it in a sandbox with time and memory limits, and renders it natively: WebGL2 and WebXR on the web, Filament and Scene Viewer on Android, RealityKit and Quick Look on iOS and visionOS. Its browser playgrounds edit scenes and export GLB, USDZ and AR in one tap with no build. Apache-2.0, free; introduced on the Google Open Source Blog Nov 3 (v1.2.0). Developer preview (alpha) and "not an officially supported Google product"; you bring the model that writes the Three.js. Found 2026-11-04.
- [Recto](https://recto.design): Free desktop design canvas for coding agents (Mac, Windows, Linux): it detects Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or OpenCode on your machine and runs them inside the app, so you can prompt a UI, motion, SVG or 3D design, then drag, resize and restyle it with the mouse, pin comments for the agent and reprompt. Designs are real HTML and CSS you can export; no MCP or API setup, everything runs locally. Shown on Show HN Nov 3 (v0.1.6, released Oct 29). Early: the app is not open source, its terms page is still "coming soon", and you need your own coding agent. Found 2026-11-04.
- [Claude Animated Shorts](https://github.com/mromidev/claude-animated-shorts): Claude Code skill that makes 55-70 second vertical cartoon story shorts (2D characters in a painted 3D world, gliding cameras, synthesized music and sound effects) by writing a three.js scene and rendering it with Remotion on your own PC, with no AI video generator. Ships the full source of its example short. MIT, free; created Nov 1 and past 850 GitHub stars in two days. You need Node, Python, ffmpeg and Remotion (Remotion has its own license: free for individuals and small teams, larger companies need a paid license), and you bring your own voice-over. Found 2026-11-03.
- [UNCUT](https://github.com/Balanov/uncut): A 7 MB headless coding-agent harness for scripts, CI and experiments: one static Go binary, four tools (read, write, replace, run a command), plain stdin/stdout or NDJSON events. It never summarizes or trims context, and stops with an error instead of passing off a cut-off answer as success. Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint or a local model, no telemetry. MIT, free; v0.1 released Nov 2, about 580 GitHub stars. Not a sandbox: shell commands run as your user, so use a container for untrusted tasks. Found 2026-11-03.
- [Flockbay](https://flockbay.com/): Desktop AI game maker built on the official Godot engine (Windows, macOS, Linux): its AI writes GDScript and scenes into a normal Godot 4 project on your disk, runs and playtests the game and fixes what breaks, and Claude Code, Codex or Cursor can drive it over MCP. Launched on Product Hunt Nov 2. Free download with no card; free hosted AI to start (needs an account) or free on your own Claude/ChatGPT plan or API key; paid plans from $20/month add hosted usage. The app itself is not open source. Found 2026-11-03.
